subject: mathematics
question_text: If a = i + 2j − 3k and b = 3i − j + 2k, then show that a+b and a−b are perpendicular to each other.

mark_split.label: Show the dot product is zero

recall_prompt: Say how you would show two vectors are perpendicular.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find a+b and a−b
steps.margin_note: First mark. Add and subtract componentwise. Both results are needed before any test can be applied.
steps.memory_tip: Add and subtract componentwise. Both results are needed before any test can be applied.

recall.must_convey: That a+b and a−b are computed componentwise, giving 4i + j − k and −2i + 3j − 5k.
accept: add and subtract componentwise to get four i plus j minus k and minus two i plus three j minus five k
work out the sum and the difference first
find a plus b and a minus b
compute both the sum and the difference

steps.why: The question is about two NEW vectors built from a and b. They have to exist before they can be tested.
common_mistakes: Sign slip where a negative meets a negative.

steps.label: Show the dot product is zero
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Perpendicular means dot product zero — that is the definition, and computing it is the whole proof.
steps.memory_tip: Perpendicular means dot product zero — computing it IS the whole proof.

recall.must_convey: That the dot product of the two results is computed and comes to zero, which is what proves they are perpendicular.
accept: dot them together and it comes to zero so they are perpendicular
minus eight plus three plus five is zero so the vectors are at right angles
the scalar product vanishes so they are perpendicular
dot product zero vasthundi kabatti perpendicular
compute the dot product and show it is zero
heard_as: minus eight plus three plus five

steps.why: A dot product is |a||b|cos θ, so it is zero exactly when cos θ is zero — that is, when the angle is 90°.
